cards.text: It's the first day of the second month, in the second year since Israel came out of Egypt. The LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, in the Tent of Meeting. And friend, He's about to hand out the BIGGEST counting job I have ever heard of.

cards.question: The LORD speaks to Moses in the Tent of Meeting. Where is Israel camped right now?

cards.text: God tells Moses to take a census of the whole congregation of Israel, by their clans and families. And this is NOT a quick wave-your-hand-and-guess headcount.

cards.question: For this census, God wants every man listed by ___, one by one.
Not everybody in Israel makes this census list. Who does God want counted?

answers.text: Men twenty or older who can serve in the army
Men thirty or older who can serve at the tent
Every firstborn son from every single family

cards.question: True or false: God tells Moses to run this whole census by himself.

cards.text: Then God names the helpers, the leader of each tribe, from Elizur of Reuben all the way down to Ahira of Naphtali. Joseph doesn't get one name on the list. He gets TWO: a leader for Ephraim and a leader for Manasseh, the sons of Joseph. And no, friend, there is no spelling quiz. I checked.
So Moses and Aaron take these leaders, the ones named by name, and get to work.

cards.question: True or false: Moses and Aaron gather the whole congregation on the first day of the second month, the same date the LORD gave the order.

cards.text: Then the counting starts, tribe by tribe, name by name, beginning with Reuben, the firstborn of Israel. Judah comes in biggest at 74,600, and Manasseh comes in smallest at 32,200. Friend, I once lost count of the chocolate chips in ONE batch. These men are counting a NATION.
Add it all up, and the total is 603,550 men. Six hundred THOUSAND. But hold on, because one tribe isn't in that number at all.

cards.question: The tribe of ___ is not numbered along with the other Israelites.

cards.text: The LORD had already told Moses, "Do not number the tribe of Levi in the census with the other Israelites." Nobody forgot them. God's got a different job for them.

cards.question: Instead of counting the Levites, what does God appoint them over?

answers.text: The tabernacle and everything in it
The army and all its divisions
The census and all its records

cards.question: True or false: When the tabernacle moves, the Levites take it down, but the other tribes set it back up.

cards.text: This is the tabernacle of the Testimony, and it is not a place for an outsider to wander up to. This is WAY past a little Staff Only sign on a door.

cards.question: What happens to an outsider who goes near the tabernacle?

answers.text: He must be put to death
He must wash and wait until evening
He must bring a lamb to the priest

cards.question: The Levites camp around the tabernacle. How does God tell the rest of the Israelites to camp?

answers.text: By divisions under their own standards
All together right around the tabernacle
Wherever each family chooses to settle

cards.question: The Levites camp around the tabernacle and watch over it, so that no ___ will fall on the congregation of Israel.
True or false: The Israelites do everything just as the LORD commanded Moses.

findings.problem: Aaron appears here for the first time with no word on who he is. Card 6 only implies helpers, and card 8 names "Moses and Aaron" without introducing Aaron.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card is not the opening card and not a long-stretch summary, but it has 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the quote, "Nobody forgot them." and "God's got a different job for them."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup says "The Levites camp around the tabernacle" and then asks how "the rest" camp. That contrast rules out the wrong answer "All together right around the tabernacle."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: No earlier card mentions the army or an age, so the baker can't reason between "twenty or older who can serve in the army" and "thirty or older who can serve at the tent." It comes down to luck. Cards 2 and 12 are already discovery questions. Card 3 could set up the census's army purpose.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The right answer (True) depends on the date the LORD gave the order, which comes from Numbers 1:1. The card cites only Numbers 1:18.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: This long-stretch summary card has 5 sentences, and card 10 has 4. The doc says every non-opening story card is 1 to 2 sentences, but its own Genesis 5 example of a good summary card has 4 sentences.
findings.question: Do summary story cards for long stretches have a sentence limit beyond the 1 to 2 rule, and if so, what is it?

findings.problem: The joke "there is no spelling quiz. I checked." refers to what the lesson will and won't ask. That sits close to talking about how lessons are made.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin joke about the lesson's own questions or quizzes, such as saying there's no quiz on a name list, or does that count as talking about the app and how lessons are made?
